summary: Guang Xing works in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London (SOAS) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett (~1998–2002). His appointments include the University of Hong Kong (~2003) and the University of British Columbia (2007, ~2011–2012).

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1982–2000) and as a professor at Shanghai Normal University (~2000).
Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He worked as a teacher at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and was appointed professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1940–1946) and with Kodo Sawaki (~1940–1965). Outside academia, he held positions at the Ministry of the Treasury and Japan Securities Finance.

Gudrun Bühnemann is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bonn, Münster, and Vienna (doctoral studies under Ernst Steinkellner, ~1978–1980). She held research posts at Pune, Nagoya, Kyoto, and Bhandarkar, and became a professor at Wisconsin-Madison (1992).

Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctorate at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (PhD completed by 2006/2010), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Jens-Uwe Hartmann.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts attested in 1991 and 2008 at the University of Ceylon.

Guo Jun works in Buddhist studies, having studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney. Trained under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin, he served as abbot at Mahabodhi Monastery (attested 2013).
Guohui Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Rissho University (~1997–2005) under Kenyu Mitomo, while also training under Sheng Yen (~1985–2009) and several other teachers.

Gurinder Singh Mann is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the English and Foreign Languages University and Harvard University (~1984–1993). He held positions at Columbia University (~1988–1999) and UC Santa Barbara (~1999).

Gustaaf Houtman works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London by 1990 under Richard Burghart, and later served there as a Senior Teaching Fellow in Anthropology and Sociology (attested 2014).

Gustav Haloun was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady (~1918–1923). He held posts at Charles University (~1928–1931), the University of Göttingen (~1931–1938), and served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Cambridge (~1938–1951).

Gustav Roth was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Munich (1949–1952) and studied at Patna University. He held posts at Göttingen (1965), ANU (1982), and was Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Guy Claxton is a scholar in education and Buddhist studies. He served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol (~1996–2008) and founded Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry.

Guy G. Stroumsa specializes in religious studies and history/archaeology. After studying at Hebrew University (~1969–1974) and Harvard (~1974–1978), he held positions at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1978–2009) and the University of Oxford (~2009–2013).

Guy Newland specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (1988) under Jeffrey Hopkins, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Gyatsho Tshering was a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and served as its director (~1972–1998).

Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Tendai Sect University. He served as president of Taisho University (~1926), professor at the University of Tokyo (1928), and lecturer at Toyo University.
Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1968–1977). He subsequently served at Rissho University as an assistant professor (~1983–1993) and professor (~1993).
Gyosho Takahashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).
